text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers often refactor to make their code easier to read and understand. This is important because clean code is simpler to maintain and update. Over time, quick fixes and poor design choices create technical debt, which makes a project harder to work with. Refactoring helps reduce this debt by reorganising the code and removing unnecessary complexity. The key rule is that the program's behaviour must stay the same. Users should not notice any difference, but developers will benefit from clearer, more organised code that is easier to work with in the future.
